llm.summary: The skill’s requirements and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (calling an external IT risk assessment API with a single API key via curl); nothing requested or instructed appears disproportionate or unrelated.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim an IT risk assessment service; declared requirement is a single TOOLWEB_API_KEY and curl — both are expected for a simple HTTP API client. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to collect user-provided maturity ratings and POST them to https://portal.toolweb.in/apis/security/it-risk-assessment using X-API-Key. Instructions do not ask the agent to read local files, other env vars, or system state outside the declared API key.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files — the skill is instruction-only and relies on curl already present. This is the lowest-risk install pattern and consistent with the stated behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only TOOLWEB_API_KEY is required and declared as the primary credential; that is proportionate for a third-party API. No additional secrets or unrelated environment variables are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system-level changes or broader privileges. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not excessive here given the skill's scope.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent, but it will send whatever answers you provide to portal.toolweb.in and requires your TOOLWEB_API_KEY. Only install/use it if you trust that service: verify the domain, HTTPS, and the provider’s privacy/security practices. Avoid submitting sensitive secrets or internal identifiers in the assessment inputs; test with non-sensitive data first. Use an API key with least privilege if possible, monitor API usage, and rotate the key if you suspect misuse.
